key_insight: A unified finite-strain thermo-mechanical variational model can predict glass additive manufacturing by coupling heat flow, phase transformations, and viscous deformation.
engineering_relevance: It helps anticipate residual stress, warpage, and microstructure evolution in printed glass, which are critical for part quality and reliability.
method: Derived from the extended Hamilton principle for coupled thermal-mechanical-phase fields
Includes first-order melting and second-order glass transition with thermal expansion, density change, and viscoelasticity
Uses a temperature-dependent viscosity law and monolithic NEM heat solution; validated in ANSYS deposition simulations
evidence_signal: The abstract reports material-point tests reproducing Time-Temperature-Transformation behavior and 3D finite element simulations showing residual stress buildup and macroscopic warpage.
watch_item: The approach is computationally involved and depends on accurate phase-kinetic and viscosity calibration for the specific glass and process window.
paper_title: First- and Second-Order Phase Transformation Modeling Based on the Hamilton Principle: A Coupled Thermo-Mechanical Approach for Glass Additive Manufacturing
